summary: Do not use. Affected by CVE-2026-93753 (CVSS 8.7), the fix PR was closed unmerged, no release since March 2023, and npm audit does not flag it.
reasoning: CVE-2026-93753: mergeObject() decides safety by inspecting the target instead of the key, so a __proto__ key survives when the target is a null-prototype object, contains a null/undefined placeholder, or already has an own __proto__ key. The returned object then inherits attacker-chosen data properties.
Reproduced all four variants locally; merged.session.isAdmin returned true while Object.keys() and JSON.stringify() showed nothing.
No fix: PR #274 was closed unmerged on 2026-09-24 and master still contains the vulnerable guard. The maintainer declined to act on issue #273.
npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities for 4.3.1 because the OSV record has only a GIT range and no npm ecosystem entry.
Last release 4.3.1 in March 2023; 22 open PRs, 18 stale; no CI and no provenance.
Slowest candidate at ~107k ops/s and stack-overflows on deep or cyclic input.
caveats: Even a patched fork would still leave the package unmaintained. Treat it as end-of-life.
Migrating away is a small change: the API is merge(target, source) with an options object.
